library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)

library(ggplot2)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sharma_2016_doxycycline_mouse"))$reference`
* Description (doxycycline): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sharma_2016_doxycycline_mouse"))$description`
* Description (minocycline): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Sharma_2016_minocycline_mouse"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1038/srep23458> (open access)
* Corrigendum: <https://doi.org/10.1038/srep46934> (corrects an author's name
  only; no value changes)

This is a **preclinical (mouse)** model. Sharma and colleagues compared two
tetracyclines, doxycycline and minocycline, as anti-Wolbachia drugs against the
human lymphatic filarial nematode *Brugia malayi* in BALB/c SCID mice. Killing
the worms' Wolbachia endosymbionts blocks embryogenesis and slowly kills the
adult worms, so the pharmacodynamic endpoint is the percentage depletion of
Wolbachia (wsp gene copies per adult female worm) relative to vehicle-treated
mice.

Each drug was fitted separately in Pmetrics (non-parametric adaptive grid) with
the same structure, so the library carries one model file per drug:

* **PK** (Methods eq. 1a/1b): one compartment with first-order oral absorption,
  CL/F and V/F per kg (Table 2).
* **PD** (Methods eq. 2a/2b/3): an effect compartment that exchanges drug
  *amount* with the central compartment at rate constants `K12` (in) and `K21`
  (out) (Table 4), and an Emax model of the effect-site concentration
  `X3 / Vf`. EC50 is fixed to the in vitro EC50 against Wolbachia-infected
  C6/36 insect cells (Table 1, Table 4) and Emax to 99.999 %. The effect-site
  volume `Vf` is "proportional to the volume of distribution of the central
  compartment".

The paper reports neither the absorption rate constant nor the `Vf / V`
proportionality constant. Both were recovered from the paper's own results:
`ka` from the median profiles of Figure 1 and `Vf / V` from the area-under-the-
PD-curve ratio of Table 4. Both derivations are reproduced below.

```{r models}
mod_dox <- readModelDb("Sharma_2016_doxycycline_mouse")
mod_min <- readModelDb("Sharma_2016_minocycline_mouse")
mods <- list(Doxycycline = mod_dox, Minocycline = mod_min)

# Both models have two outputs (Cc and wolbachia_reduction), so observation
# rows sit on the central ODE state and carry dvid = 1; rxode2 returns both
# outputs as columns on every observation row.
make_ev <- function(dose, ii, n_dose, obs_times, n_id = 1) {
  one <- data.frame(
    time = c(0, obs_times), amt = c(dose, rep(NA, length(obs_times))),
    ii = c(ii, rep(0, length(obs_times))), addl = c(n_dose - 1, rep(0, length(obs_times))),
    evid = c(1L, rep(0L, length(obs_times))),
    cmt = c("depot", rep("central", length(obs_times))),
    dvid = c(NA_integer_, rep(1L, length(obs_times)))
  )
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n_id), function(i) cbind(id = i, one)))
}
```

# Population

All animals were male BALB/c SCID mice. The PK study used uninfected mice
weighing 24-28 g, given 25 mg/kg of either drug by oral gavage, with rich
tail-vein microsampling (20 uL whole blood) up to 8 h after a single dose and on
day 7 of once-daily dosing; Table 2 reports the day-7 fit. The PD studies
infected mice intraperitoneally with 100 *B. malayi* L3 larvae and started oral
dosing 6 weeks later: 25 mg/kg once or twice daily for 7 to 42 days, and for
minocycline also 25, 40 or 80 mg/kg twice daily for 7 days. In the Figure 3
studies mice were necropsied 12 weeks after infection (so after a washout of
up to 35 days); in the Figure 4 study adult worms were recovered immediately
after the last dose. Each arm had 4-13 mice and 10-40 adult female worms
assayed by qPCR (Table 3; Figure 3 and 4 legends). The number of PK mice is not
stated. The same facts are in each model's `population` metadata.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Doxycycline | Minocycline | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| One-compartment oral PK | -- | -- | Methods eq. 1a, 1b |
| Effect compartment exchanging amount with central | -- | -- | Methods eq. 2a, 2b |
| `effect = Emax * (X3/Vf) / (EC50 + X3/Vf)` | -- | -- | Methods eq. 3 |
| `lcl` (CL/F, L/h/kg) | 1.2 | 3.2 | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (V/F, L/kg) | 6.9 | 13.2 | Table 2 |
| `etalcl` (variance) | 0.10536 | 0.0087507 | Table 2 SD 0.4 / 0.3, as `log(1 + CV^2)` |
| `etalvc` (variance) | 0.27723 | 0.10995 | Table 2 SD 3.9 / 4.5, as `log(1 + CV^2)` |
| `lka` (1/h) | 2.53 | 3.62 | **Not reported**; digitised from Figure 1 (below) |
| `lk1e` (K12, 1/h) | 4.36e-7 | 1.08e-5 | Table 4 |
| `lke1` (K21, 1/h) | 8.06e-4 | 1.49e-3 | Table 4 |
| `lec50` (nM, fixed) | 15.32 | 11.75 | Table 4; Table 1 (in vitro) |
| `lemax` (%, fixed) | 99.999 | 99.999 | Methods, PK/PD modelling |
| `lveff_ratio` (Vf / V, fixed) | 0.023 | 0.023 | **Not reported**; back-solved from Table 4 AUC_PD ratio (below) |
| Molecular weight (g/mol) | 444.43 | 457.48 | Free base, used to convert mg/L to nM |
| `propSd`, `addSd_wolbachia_reduction` | fixed 0 | fixed 0 | Not reported |

# Absorption rate constant from Figure 1

Figure 1 plots the median day-7 profile of 1000 simulated mice after 25 mg/kg
once daily. Digitised against the axis ticks, the median peaks at 3.02 ug/mL
(doxycycline) and 1.57 ug/mL (minocycline), at about 1.1 h. With the Table 2
CL/F and V/F, `ka` = 2.53 1/h and 3.62 1/h reproduce those peaks. The
deterministic check below confirms the packaged values do.

```{r ka-check}
pk_times <- 144 + c(seq(0, 3, by = 0.01), seq(3.25, 24, by = 0.25))
ev_pk <- make_ev(dose = 25, ii = 24, n_dose = 7, obs_times = pk_times)

typ_pk <- bind_rows(lapply(names(mods), function(drug) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mods[[drug]]), ev_pk)) |>
    mutate(drug = drug)
}))
typ_peak <- typ_pk |>
  group_by(drug) |>
  summarise(cmax = max(Cc), tmax = time[which.max(Cc)] - 144, .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(typ_peak, digits = 3, caption = "Typical-value day-7 peak, 25 mg/kg once daily.")

# Deterministic: the digitised Figure 1 median peaks are 3.02 and 1.57 ug/mL.
stopifnot(
  abs(typ_peak$cmax[typ_peak$drug == "Doxycycline"] / 3.02 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(typ_peak$cmax[typ_peak$drug == "Minocycline"] / 1.57 - 1) < 0.01
)
```

Matching the peak *height* sets `ka`; the peak *time* is then about 1.1 h for
doxycycline and 0.8 h for minocycline, against about 1.1 h for both in the
figure. A Pmetrics typical value is the mean of a non-parametric marginal
distribution rather than the parameters of any one mouse, so peak time is not
used as a gate. `ka` has almost no influence on the PD: the AUC_PD ratio of
Table 4 changes by less than 0.001 for `ka` anywhere between 2 and 5 1/h.

# Replicate Figure 1: day-7 PK profiles

```{r vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160321)
vpc <- bind_rows(lapply(names(mods), function(drug) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[drug]], make_ev(25, 24, 7, pk_times, n_id = 200))) |>
    mutate(drug = drug)
}))
vpc_sum <- vpc |>
  mutate(tad = time - 144) |>
  group_by(drug, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(tad)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p05), linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p95), linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~drug, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Blood concentration (ug/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Sharma 2016: median and 5th / 95th percentiles of 200 simulated mice."
  )

# Peak of each percentile curve, against the peaks digitised from Figure 1.
vpc_sum |>
  group_by(drug) |>
  summarise(across(c(p05, p50, p95), max), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    fig1_p05 = c(1.9, 0.93), fig1_p50 = c(3.02, 1.57), fig1_p95 = c(9.3, 3.2)
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Drug = drug, `5th pct` = p05, Median = p50, `95th pct` = p95,
    `Fig. 1 5th pct` = fig1_p05, `Fig. 1 median` = fig1_p50, `Fig. 1 95th pct` = fig1_p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Peak concentration (ug/mL) of each percentile curve: 200 simulated mice vs. Figure 1 (digitised).")
```

The table above shows how far the simulated percentile bands match the
published ones. The published 95th percentile at the peak is the furthest off.
The non-parametric fit also had between-mouse variability in `ka`, which the
paper does not report and the model therefore does not carry.

# PKNCA validation against Table 2

Table 2 gives the day-7 mean AUC over the 24 h dosing interval and the mean
half-life. Means of a cohort are compared with means, so the simulated PKNCA
results are averaged before going into the comparison table.

```{r pknca}
stopifnot(!anyNA(vpc$Cc))
nca_in <- vpc |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(treatment = drug) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_in, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- nca_in |>
  distinct(treatment, id) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 144, by = 24)) |>
  mutate(amt = 25)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 144, end = 168,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

sim_means <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "half.life")) |>
  group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(PPORRES = mean(PPORRES), .groups = "drop")

published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~auclast, ~half.life,
  "Doxycycline", 22.8, 4.4,
  "Minocycline", 8.4, 3.0
)
cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_means,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(auclast = "h*ug/mL", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated cohort means vs. Sharma 2016 Table 2 (day 7). * differs by >20%.")
attr(cmp, "footnote")

auc_sim <- sim_means |> filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast")
# The mean AUC of a cohort follows the dose / CL/F of every mouse, so a
# mistyped clearance, dose or unit moves it by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  abs(auc_sim$PPORRES[auc_sim$treatment == "Doxycycline"] / 22.8 - 1) < 0.15,
  abs(auc_sim$PPORRES[auc_sim$treatment == "Minocycline"] / 8.4 - 1) < 0.15
)
```

The mean AUCs agree closely with Table 2. That is expected: the mean of
`25 / CL` over a log-normal CL/F with the Table 2 CV is 23.1 and
7.9 h.ug/mL. The mean half-lives come out somewhat longer than Table 2's
4.4 and 3.0 h, because a log-normal V/F with a 56 % CV has a long upper
tail. Table 2's half-life SDs (3.7 and 2.3 h) are wider than the CL/F
and V/F SDs alone can produce, and the paper does not give the joint
distribution, so the half-life is not gated.

# Effect-site volume from Table 4

Table 4 gives the ratio of the area under the PD curve (percentage Wolbachia
depletion integrated over 0-28 days) for minocycline to doxycycline after
25 mg/kg twice daily for 28 days: 1.7. This is the fitted model's own output,
so it fixes the one structural constant the paper leaves out, `Vf / V`.
The constant is assumed to be the same for both drugs, since the paper states
one rule for both. The scan below shows how the ratio depends on it.

```{r auc-pd-ratio}
ev_bid28 <- make_ev(dose = 25, ii = 12, n_dose = 56, obs_times = seq(0, 672, by = 0.25))

auc_pd <- function(mod, ratio) {
  m <- rxode2::ini(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), lveff_ratio = log(ratio))
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(m, ev_bid28))
  c(
    auc = sum(diff(s$time) * (head(s$wolbachia_reduction, -1) + tail(s$wolbachia_reduction, -1)) / 2),
    end = tail(s$wolbachia_reduction, 1)
  )
}
scan <- bind_rows(lapply(c(0.003, 0.006, 0.01, 0.02, 0.023, 0.025, 0.03, 0.1, 1), function(r) {
  a <- auc_pd(mod_dox, r)
  b <- auc_pd(mod_min, r)
  data.frame(
    `Vf / V` = r, `Doxycycline day-28 depletion (%)` = a[["end"]],
    `Minocycline day-28 depletion (%)` = b[["end"]], `AUC_PD ratio` = b[["auc"]] / a[["auc"]],
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
knitr::kable(scan, digits = 3, caption = "AUC_PD ratio (minocycline / doxycycline, 0-28 days, 25 mg/kg bid) by Vf / V.")

# Packaged value: the ratio is printed to two significant figures, so 1.7
# stands for 1.65-1.75. The solves are deterministic.
ratio_pkg <- scan$`AUC_PD ratio`[scan$`Vf / V` == 0.023]
stopifnot(ratio_pkg > 1.65, ratio_pkg < 1.75)
# Section 'Pharmacokinetic-Pharmacokinetic modelling': transfer into the effect
# site is 24-fold faster for minocycline.
k12_fold <- 1.08e-5 / 4.36e-7
stopifnot(abs(k12_fold - 24) < 1)
```

The ratio is 1.70 at `Vf / V` = 0.023 (1.65 at 0.021, 1.75 at 0.025), and
falls to about 1 at small values, where both drugs saturate. The value is
close to the body weight of a 25 g mouse in kg. One possible explanation, which
the paper does not confirm, is that the authors' code divided a per-kg amount
by `V` in L/kg times body weight.

# Observed vs. predicted Wolbachia depletion

The model's typical-value predictions are set against the median depletions
reported in the Results text, at the time the worms were recovered: day 42
after the start of dosing for Figure 3 (12 weeks after infection) and the end
of dosing for Figure 4.

```{r pd-obs}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~drug, ~dose, ~ii, ~days, ~read_day, ~observed, ~source,
  "Doxycycline", 25, 24, 42, 42, 66.30, "Fig. 3b",
  "Doxycycline", 25, 12, 28, 42, 90.35, "Fig. 3b",
  "Minocycline", 25, 24, 28, 42, 85.08, "Fig. 3b",
  "Minocycline", 25, 12, 28, 42, 99.51, "Fig. 3b",
  "Minocycline", 25, 12, 7, 7, NA, "Fig. 4b (71.65-84.08 across 25-80 mg/kg)",
  "Minocycline", 80, 12, 7, 7, NA, "Fig. 4b (71.65-84.08 across 25-80 mg/kg)",
  "Minocycline", 25, 12, 14, 14, 94.93, "Fig. 4b",
  "Minocycline", 25, 12, 28, 28, 98.17, "Fig. 4b"
)
pred_one <- function(drug, dose, ii, days, read_day) {
  ev <- make_ev(dose, ii, days * 24 / ii, read_day * 24)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mods[[drug]]), ev))
  tail(s$wolbachia_reduction, 1)
}
regimens$predicted <- mapply(pred_one, regimens$drug, regimens$dose, regimens$ii,
                             regimens$days, regimens$read_day)
regimens |>
  mutate(regimen = paste0(dose, " mg/kg ", ifelse(ii == 12, "bid", "qd"), " x ", days, " d")) |>
  select(drug, regimen, read_day, observed, predicted, source) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Drug = drug, Regimen = regimen, `Read day` = read_day,
    `Observed median (%)` = observed, `Predicted (%)` = predicted, Source = source
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Wolbachia depletion: observed medians vs. typical-value prediction.")
```

```{r pd-curves, fig.height = 4}
curve_one <- function(drug, dose, ii, days) {
  ev <- make_ev(dose, ii, days * 24 / ii, seq(0, 42 * 24, by = 6))
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mods[[drug]]), ev)) |>
    mutate(drug = drug, regimen = paste0(dose, " mg/kg ", ifelse(ii == 12, "bid", "qd"), " x ", days, " d"))
}
curves <- bind_rows(
  curve_one("Doxycycline", 25, 12, 28), curve_one("Doxycycline", 25, 24, 42),
  curve_one("Minocycline", 25, 12, 28), curve_one("Minocycline", 25, 24, 28)
)
pts <- regimens |>
  filter(!is.na(observed), read_day == 42) |>
  mutate(regimen = paste0(dose, " mg/kg ", ifelse(ii == 12, "bid", "qd"), " x ", days, " d"))
ggplot(curves, aes(time / 24, wolbachia_reduction, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(read_day, observed), size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~drug) +
  labs(
    x = "Days from first dose", y = "Wolbachia depletion (%)", colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical-value predictions; points are the observed medians at necropsy (Figure 3b)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The model ranks the regimens as the paper does: minocycline beats doxycycline
at every matched regimen, and twice-daily dosing beats once-daily dosing. The
once-daily regimens read at necropsy are close to the observed medians (62 %
against 66 % for doxycycline over 42 days, 88 % against 85 % for minocycline
over 28 days). The twice-daily 28-day regimens are underestimated: 66 %
against 90 % for doxycycline and 94 % against 99.5 % for minocycline. The
7-day minocycline arms of Figure 4 are overestimated (89-96 % against
72-84 %). The Wolbachia effect is slow to build and slow to decay, so the
day-42 prediction after a 28-day course is the day-28 value decaying through
a 14-day washout.

A smaller `Vf / V` would raise the twice-daily predictions: at 0.006 the
day-28 depletion is 91 % (doxycycline) and 99 % (minocycline), close to the
observations. But the AUC_PD ratio then falls to 1.24, against Table 4's 1.7
(see the scan above), and the once-daily and 7-day arms would be
overestimated further. No single value reproduces all of these. The packaged
model is tied to Table 4 because Table 4 is the fitted model's own output,
while the observations are medians of worms pooled across mice. The
published `K12` / `K21` summarise non-parametric distributions, so a
typical-value solve need not match the observed medians.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **`ka` is digitised, not reported.** It was set so the typical-value day-7
  peak equals the median peak of Figure 1 (3.02 and 1.57 ug/mL). The paper
  printed no value, and no between-mouse variability is carried on it.
* **`Vf / V` = 0.023 is back-solved, not reported.** It comes from the
  Table 4 AUC_PD ratio of 1.7, assuming the same constant for both drugs. The
  ratio is printed to two significant figures, so 0.021-0.025 is equally
  consistent.
* **The units of `K12` / `K21` are not printed.** They are read as 1/h, the
  time unit of the PK model. Per day would give doxycycline an effect-site
  half-life of 860 days.
* **The effect compartment is fed by the central amount**, as Methods eq. 2a/2b
  print it (drug leaves central at `K12 * X2`). This removes a negligible
  amount from the central compartment (`K12` is under 0.005 % of the
  elimination rate constant).
* **Between-mouse variability is approximated.** Pmetrics estimates a
  non-parametric distribution, and Table 2 reports only means and SDs. CL/F and
  V/F carry log-normal variability with the same CV, centred on the reported
  means. No variability is carried on `ka`, `K12` or `K21`, which the paper
  does not report.
* **No residual error.** The Pmetrics assay-error polynomial is not reported,
  so both residual SDs are fixed to zero.
* **Molecular weights.** The nM EC50 is compared with the effect-site
  concentration converted at the free-base molecular weight (444.43 and
  457.48 g/mol). The salt form dosed is not stated. The doses are applied as
  printed.
* **Output name.** The depletion output `wolbachia_reduction` (a percentage of
  the vehicle control) has no registered canonical name. It is declared in
  `paper_specific_compartments`; a second model of this endpoint would justify
  registering it.
* **Parameter names.** `lk1e` / `lke1` follow the existing models that carry an
  asymmetric amount-transfer effect compartment (`Valade_2015_emtricitabine`,
  `Groenendaal_2007_morphine_rat_eeg`); `K12` / `K21` are not used because those
  names are reserved for central-peripheral PK distribution. `lveff_ratio`
  follows the shape of `lvp_ratio` (a fraction of the central volume).
* **Text typos.** The Results text gives V/F in "L/hr" (Table 2 has L/kg). It
  also gives once- and twice-daily 25 mg/kg daily exposures of 22.8 / 40.6
  (doxycycline) and 7.8 / 14.9 (minocycline) ug.h/mL. A linear model gives
  exactly twice the once-daily value for twice-daily dosing, and Table 2
  reports 8.4, not 7.8, for minocycline. Neither affects a model parameter.
* **Not reproduced.** The human profiles of Figure 2 come from earlier
  published human models whose parameters this paper does not print. The
  microfilarial counts of Figure 3c were not modelled.
